articles.excerpt: One of the most surprising parts of modern Linux gaming is that a Windows-only Steam game may launch without a Windows installation. Steam’s compatibility tool, Proton, makes that possible for many ti…
articles.body: One of the most surprising parts of modern Linux gaming is that a Windows-only Steam game may launch without a Windows installation. Steam’s compatibility tool, Proton, makes that possible for many titles. The basic setup is often simple, but a few good habits can save you from confusing troubleshooting later. This guide walks through a cautious first run: install Steam from a trusted source, use the default compatibility setting, test one game, and only then investigate alternatives. Menu names can move between Steam versions and distributions, so treat the instructions as a route rather than an exact screenshot-by-screenshot promise.

articles.title: How to build a Hyperliquid trading bot without keeping the private key on your server
articles.excerpt: To run a Hyperliquid trading bot without keeping a private key on your server, have a Lit Action sign the bot's orders with a Lit wallet. The wallet's key is created inside a secure enclave and stays…
articles.body: To run a Hyperliquid trading bot without keeping a private key on your server, have a Lit Action sign the bot's orders with a Lit wallet. The wallet's key is created inside a secure enclave and stays there. Your main Hyperliquid account approves the wallet's address as an API wallet. A Lit Action, which is a JavaScript function that runs in the same enclave, checks every order against limits written into its code before it signs. Your server holds a Lit usage key that can only run that action with that wallet. Why an API wallet Hyperliquid lets your main account approve a separate API wallet to sign on its behalf. The API wallet holds no funds of its own, but it can trade the funds in your main account.

articles.title: How do I get ChatGPT responses programmatically without using the OpenAI API?
articles.excerpt: Drive ChatGPT's web app with a browser automation library such as Playwright, or call a scraping API that runs that browser for you. Both give you what ChatGPT shows a visitor, and that is a different…
articles.body: Drive ChatGPT's web app with a browser automation library such as Playwright, or call a scraping API that runs that browser for you. Both give you what ChatGPT shows a visitor, and that is a different result from what the OpenAI API returns for the same prompt. A short Playwright script works, with one condition. On 16 November 2026 a headed Chromium got ChatGPT's logged-out page and a full answer with its links. A headless Chromium got Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page with HTTP 403. The page has few stable hooks. The answer's elements carry generated class names such as x78zum5 . The fixed hooks we found were a form field name and two aria-label values. The API and the web app cite different pages.

articles.title: One memory for Claude and ChatGPT
articles.excerpt: If you use Claude and ChatGPT for work, you know the routine: every new chat starts blank, and you explain who you are, how you work and what the project is about. Again. Alter Ego is a small connecto…
articles.body: If you use Claude and ChatGPT for work, you know the routine: every new chat starts blank, and you explain who you are, how you work and what the project is about. Again. Alter Ego is a small connector that gives all your AI chats one shared memory. What you tell one assistant about yourself and your work, the others remember too. What it does Keeps your rules, your profile and a log of your work in one place. Stores everything as plain files in your own OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, GitHub or Azure DevOps, so you can read, edit or delete it yourself. Is not tied to one AI vendor: your memory stays yours. Where it works It works in Claude and ChatGPT today. You add it as a custom connector (ChatGPT asks for the server URL and OAuth, Claude has its own connector screen).

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.body: On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster . The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.

articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase.

articles.body: As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big. The company recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower. It was a huge moment for SpaceX , bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship. "Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15).

articles.title: What exactly is a light-day? Here's what Voyager 1's latest milestone means for the interstellar probe
articles.excerpt: Voyager 1 is approaching a distance of one light-day from Earth, a milestone that highlights the enormous distances involved in deep-space exploration.
articles.body: After nearly 50 years traveling through space, NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is approaching a milestone no human-made object has reached before: a distance of one light-day from Earth. This milestone — which Voyager 1 is expected to reach on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (1016:07 GMT) — highlights the immense distances Voyager 1 has traveled and the challenges of communicating with spacecraft operating in the outer reaches of the solar system and beyond. Astronomers use a measurement known as a light-day to describe how far light travels in 24 hours. Light moves at approximately 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometers) per second, meaning one light-day is roughly 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), according to a statement from NASA.
